content.subject: Following up from MFG Ops Expo
content.body: Dana - good talking at the expo. You described the Monday spreadsheet ritual and I haven't stopped thinking about it. We built Harborview for exactly that. 30 minutes this week to see if it's a fit?

content.subject: Following up from MFG Ops Expo
content.body: Worth a look. Adding Leo Nakamura, our eng lead - anything ops adopts, he has to live with. Monday the 16th, 10am central?

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: Thanks both. Dana, you mentioned the ops team is feeling the pain most, want to start there?

transcript.speaker: Dana Whitfield
transcript.text: Sure. We run three plants and every one of them reports inventory differently. My analysts spend Mondays just normalizing spreadsheets.

transcript.speaker: Leo Nakamura
transcript.text: From my side the question is integration. We're on a mix of SAP and a homegrown WMS at the Toledo plant. What does connecting that look like?

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: SAP is a native connector. For the homegrown system we'd use the REST ingestion API, and our SE Sam would scope that with your team directly.

transcript.speaker: Dana Whitfield
transcript.text: If Monday normalization goes away, that's two heads worth of time back. I want to see this properly.

transcript.speaker: Leo Nakamura
transcript.text: Can we get API docs before a demo? I'd rather come with real questions.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: Sending them today, along with the SAP connector spec.

transcript.speaker: Dana Whitfield
transcript.text: Let's do a full demo next week. I'll bring Marcus, our CTO. He'll want to see it before we go anywhere serious.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: Perfect. I'll coordinate times over email.

content.subject: Re: Discovery call recap + API docs
content.body: Recap attached. Leo - API docs and SAP connector spec included as promised. Dana - whenever Marcus has 40 minutes, we'll run the full demo.

content.subject: Re: Discovery call recap + API docs
content.body: Docs look solid. Found two field types in our WMS payloads that won't map cleanly - details at the demo.

content.subject: Re: Discovery call recap + API docs
content.body: Marcus is in for Wednesday the 25th. Calendar invite sent.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: Marcus, welcome. Plan is a live run of the platform against a three-site inventory setup that mirrors yours.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Good. I've read Dana's summary, so assume I know the pitch. Show me the product.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: Here's the normalized view across all three sites, updating live. The Toledo-style custom source is flowing through the ingestion API.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: This is cleaner than I expected. What's the story when a source schema changes without warning? Because that happens here monthly.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: Schema drift gets quarantined, you get an alert, and the mapping editor shows you exactly what changed. Nothing silently corrupts.

transcript.speaker: Leo Nakamura
transcript.text: I tested the API docs against our WMS payloads last night. Two field types won't map cleanly, I'll send details.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: Send them over, that's exactly the kind of thing Sam will scope in a technical session.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: What's a realistic rollout timeline for three plants? I don't want a six-month professional services engagement.

transcript.speaker: Jordan Lee
transcript.text: Six to eight weeks for all three, phased. First plant live in three.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Alright. I'm interested. Dana, take this to a technical evaluation and let's see real numbers when you have them.

transcript.speaker: Dana Whitfield
transcript.text: I'll set up the technical session with Leo and Sam, and let's get a Slack channel going so this isn't all email.

content.text: As promised, one channel instead of forty email threads. Leo, Sam - it's all yours for the technical stuff.
Perfect. Leo, want to start with those two field mapping issues before our deep dive next week?
yes - biggest one is our nested BOM structure. also what are the API rate limits? toledo syncs in bursts
10k requests/min sustained, bursts to 50k. Toledo's bursts won't touch that. BOM structure let's do live on Thursday.
ran your postman collection against a staging copy. clean except the timestamp thing, curious what you'll say thursday

transcript.speaker: Sam Okafor
transcript.text: I went through the two field mapping issues you flagged. The timestamp one is solved with a transform rule, I'll show you. The nested BOM structure is the interesting one.

transcript.speaker: Leo Nakamura
transcript.text: Interesting good or interesting bad?

transcript.speaker: Sam Okafor
transcript.text: Good. The ingestion API takes nested payloads, we just flatten them with a mapping template. Here, watch.

transcript.speaker: Leo Nakamura
transcript.text: Okay, that handles it. What about backfill? We'd want two years of history loaded.

transcript.speaker: Sam Okafor
transcript.text: Bulk import handles that, two years is maybe a weekend job. We should just test it in a sandbox with your real exports.

transcript.speaker: Leo Nakamura
transcript.text: Let's do it. I can get you sanitized exports from all three plants by end of next week.

transcript.speaker: Sam Okafor
transcript.text: Then let's agree: sandbox loaded by the following Monday, and you try to break it for a week.

transcript.speaker: Leo Nakamura
transcript.text: Deal. I'm good at breaking things.

content.text: Good session today. Recap: timestamp solved with transform rule, BOM flattening template works, sandbox by the 23rd with real exports.
confirmed on all three. exports to you by end of next week

content.subject: Sanitized exports
content.body: Sam - exports from all three plants are in your secure upload. Toledo's is ugly, don't say I didn't warn you.

content.subject: Sanitized exports
content.body: Received. Toledo's is genuinely creative, but the mapper handles it. Sandbox on track for Monday.

content.subject: Vendor onboarding - procurement
content.body: Jordan - Ines Farah, procurement. Marcus asked me to start our vendor pass early. Please send: W-9, insurance certs, your standard MSA, and SOC 2 report. Standard review is two weeks.

content.subject: Vendor onboarding - procurement
content.body: All four attached. Happy to connect our legal with yours directly if anything in the MSA needs discussion.

content.text: Sandbox is live with all three plants loaded. Leo, go break it.
update: threw our worst month at it (the feb inventory count disaster). it caught every mismatch and the drift quarantine did its job when i fed it a mangled schema on purpose
That february dataset is going in our internal hall of fame.
watching this thread with joy. this is the monday ritual dying in real time

transcript.speaker: Ava Chen
transcript.text: Marcus, thanks for making time. I wanted us connected before anything hits paper.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Appreciated. The technical eval is going well from what Leo tells me. My questions are all commercial now.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Three plants now, but if this works we'd add the two Canadian sites next year. I want pricing that doesn't punish us for growing.

transcript.speaker: Ava Chen
transcript.text: That's exactly how we'd structure it, a five-site ramp with the discount locked now. Jordan will model both paths in the proposal.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Second thing: support. Toledo runs a night shift. If sync breaks at 2am, what happens?

transcript.speaker: Ava Chen
transcript.text: Enterprise tier is 24/7 with a one-hour response SLA. It's in writing in the proposal.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Good. Get us a proposal by mid-April and I'll have procurement start their pass now so legal isn't the long pole.

transcript.speaker: Ava Chen
transcript.text: You'll have it. And I'm a call away if anything needs unblocking on our side.

content.text: Great exec sync with Marcus today - proposal by mid-April with both pricing paths. Team, let's make it airtight.

content.subject: Vendor onboarding - procurement
content.body: Package looks complete. Two standard redlines on the MSA coming from legal, nothing controversial. We'll be ready when the proposal lands.

content.text: official verdict from eng: pass. told dana and marcus this morning. from my side, ship it
proposal request just went to jordan by email. excited over here

content.subject: Proposal timing
content.body: Jordan - sandbox verdict from Leo is a clear pass. Marcus wants the proposal by April 15 so we can approve before end of quarter. Both pricing paths like Ava discussed, please.

content.subject: Proposal timing
content.body: You'll have it by the 13th. Thanks for keeping this moving so cleanly, Dana.
